No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators — overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

The reviewed alerts appear to be documentation, tests, or repository hygiene controls rather than malware-like behavior.

  • .github/repo-guard.blocklist references .env, SSH keys, and certificate patterns as a **commit-prevention blocklist**, not credential theft.
  • .gitignore entries such as .env and .pypirc are **local credential ignore rules**.
  • raw.githubusercontent.com links and curl | sh snippets in README.md, PKG-INFO, and docs appear to be **installation documentation**, with no evidence that they run automatically during package installation.
  • External URLs and curl examples in .github/skills/**/SKILL.md are Markdown-based agent/skill documentation; no evidence shows execution during PyPI install or import.

Automatic Execution Paths

No malicious automatic execution path was confirmed in the provided extracted text.

  • .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py: no evidence
  • Malicious setup.py or PEP 517 build hook execution: not confirmed from provided text

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

No confirmed malicious evidence.

  • **Credential harvesting:** No broad environment-variable, SSH key, cloud credential, or token harvesting logic was identified. Sensitive paths appear in blocklist/ignore contexts.
  • **Archive staging / exfiltration:** No evidence of staging harvested files with tar/zip/base64 or uploading them externally.
  • **Persistence:** No cron/systemd/launch agent/shell profile modification evidence. “Startup” references are in MCP usability documentation.
  • **CI/cloud lateral movement:** GitHub Actions, Codecov, and PyPI trusted publishing references appear in documentation/changelog context; no token theft or workflow injection evidence was found.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** No base64/encryption/exec/eval staged loader evidence was confirmed. Pre-scan obfuscation hits appear to be false positives from German documentation terms.

No distribution-integrity anomaly plausibly indicating a malicious supply-chain attack was confirmed.

  • The sdist includes .github/, documentation, tests, playground, and audit artifacts, but the provided evidence does not show hidden payloads or automatic execution from these files.
